knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Product Containing a Trigonometric Function

question.:question/worked-solution:
Here, we have the product of the two functions $u(x)=6 x^{4}$ and $v(x)=\cos{\left(x \right)}.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}((6 x^{4})(\cos{\left(x \right)}))^{'} & =u'(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot v'(x) \\ & =(6 x^{4})'\cdot (\cos{\left(x \right)})+(6 x^{4})\cdot (\cos{\left(x \right)})' \\ & =(24 x^{3})(\cos{\left(x \right)})+(6 x^{4})(- \sin{\left(x \right)}) \\ & =- 6 x^{4} \sin{\left(x \right)} + 24 x^{3} \cos{\left(x \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}({7}^{x}\operatorname{sin}(x))^{'} & ={u}^{'}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{'}(x) \\  & =({7}^{x})^{'}\cdot \operatorname{sin}(x)+{7}^{x}\cdot (\operatorname{sin}(x))^{'} \\  & =({7}^{x}\operatorname{ln}(7))(\operatorname{sin}(x))+({7}^{x})(\operatorname{cos}(x)) \\  & ={7}^{x}\operatorname{ln}(7)\operatorname{sin}(x)+{7}^{x}\operatorname{cos}(x)\end{aligned}
$$
